sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-live-desk-2026-10-02-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx :: Quality Checks row 44 (check 43) and Internal Quality Checks row 44 (annotation: 'Gate/constraint failures hard-zero the quality terms, and passing only the cheap gates earns little.')
evidence: Source wiring conforms. tests/scoring.toml:1-3 sets render = 0.0 and constraints = 0.0 under [gates]; :5-8 weights are functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2 (sum 1.0) and name no gate; :10-11 floor functional = 0.05. tests/tools/score.py:41 gates_passed requires every gate score > 0.0; :42-44 forces all scored dimensions to 0.0 unless gates passed and a scored reward.json exists; :46 the weighted sum iterates only over [weights], so gates contribute no mass; :47-48 reward is 0.0 unless gates and the functional floor (strict >) both pass; :83 returns 1 on gate failure. tests/test.sh:212-222 runs the gates suite first, and on score.py exit 1 exits before run_suite scored at :224 (non-0/1 exit writes the plain zero record); :60 writes a zero reward before anything else. Gate judge.toml files use aggregation = "all_pass" with one binary criterion each and no weight key inside [judge]; scored suites use weighted_mean. scoring.toml, test.sh and tools/score.py are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff -q; sha256 95f70d6e..., bd682592..., 13de2b38...). Each scored prompt also carries an in-dimension backend gate that zeroes a blank/static shell (functional/prompt.md:15, polish/prompt.md:12, visual/prompt.md:12). Budgets nest: 1500 + 11100 < verifier timeout 13200 (task.toml:27). I executed the frozen score.py locally against synthetic suite outputs (evidence/43/score_policy_simulation.txt): a failed render gate with a stale all-1.0 scored file gives reward 0.0 and exit 1; gates passed with no scored suite gives 0.0; functional 0.0 or exactly 0.05 with polish and visual 1.0 gives reward 0.0 (floors_passed 0); functional 0.0526 gives 0.4316; perfect gives 1.0; a missing gate key or missing gate file exits 2. Broken-app probe: a static or browser-only shell that somehow passes both gates is still zeroed by the functional floor. Conforming-alternative probe: nothing in this row's mechanics penalises a conforming app; gate strictness itself belongs to other rows. Observation, not a defect of this row: with 152 functional criteria the 0.05 floor is cleared by roughly 8 passing criteria (if equally weighted), after which polish and visual count in full, so a thin but genuinely persisting app with good styling could reach about 0.43. That is the template's fixed floor value and shared reward policy, which this review must not alter. Risk stays true because the raw-evidence index states that full configured grading, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent: the gate-fail skip path in test.sh and the judges' application of the in-prompt gates to a weak app have not been exercised in the verifier image with the configured judge. My simulation runs only score.py on synthetic inputs on the host; it is not a verifier or judge run.
